claims.text: GHK is an endogenous human plasma tripeptide first described in 1973; GHK-Cu is its copper complex.
claims.gradeDecision: C/context — history

claims.text: Proposed mechanism: GHK-Cu modulates copper delivery to enzymes including superoxide dismutase and lysyl oxidase and activates wound-healing and antioxidant gene-expression programmes — a mechanistic claim resting on reviews by the peptide's originator.
claims.reviewNote: teach as mechanism with the conflict of interest visible
claims.gradeDecision: D — mechanism only, originator reviews; lesson must say so

claims.text: Human evidence for topical GHK-Cu is small-trial: one PubMed-indexed randomized trial (post-laser wound healing, 2006) and manufacturer-sponsored cosmetic trials that are not indexed; the guides rate the cosmetic indication GRADE C.
claims.reviewNote: grade C per both guides; Omar to confirm
claims.gradeDecision: C — one small indexed RCT + unindexed sponsor trials; matches both guides

claims.text: Injectable GHK-Cu has no randomized human trials; use rests on anecdote, and injection-site pain and rash are common.
claims.reviewNote: safety statement is the guides' clinical observation; Li 2016 is mechanistic support only
claims.gradeDecision: D — no RCTs for injectable use; irritation from the guides' clinical observation

claims.text: Whether topical GHK-Cu reaches the dermis in meaningful amounts is unsettled; penetration data are in vitro and measurement-dependent.
claims.gradeDecision: D — in vitro penetration only

claims.text: US status (as of May 14, 2026): GHK-Cu for non-injectable routes sits in FDA's 503A Category 1 (under evaluation) after its nomination was withdrawn on April 22, 2026 and partially reinstated; FDA intends to consult the PCAC on it before the end of February 2027. Category 1 is an enforcement posture, not approval; the injectable route has no such standing.
claims.reviewNote: more precise than either guide's 'Category 1 (non-injectable)'; date-stamp it in the lesson
claims.gradeDecision: regulatory record, date-stamped 2026-05-14

claims.text: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (pal-KTTKS, Matrixyl) improved photoaging measures in a 12-week randomized trial funded by the manufacturer; the Matrixyl 3000 blend rests on the maker's technical dossier, which is not indexed.

claims.gradeDecision: C for pal-KTTKS (sponsor RCT + independent 2023 RCT); D for the Matrixyl 3000 blend (dossier only)

claims.text: Argireline (acetyl hexapeptide-3/-8) mimics the N-terminus of SNAP-25; randomized placebo-controlled trials report modest wrinkle improvement, but delivery to the neuromuscular junction at cosmetic concentrations is considered implausible — the effect, if real, is not a botulinum substitute.
claims.reviewNote: PPG-Aug marks 'Wang Y et al.' as not indexed — the 2013 Am J Clin Dermatol RCT is indexed (PMID 23417317); report to the author
claims.gradeDecision: C — sponsor and independent RCTs, modest effect; NB A&RE rates C, PPG-Aug rates D — lesson states C and names the disagreement

claims.text: Leuphasyl (pentapeptide-18): the only efficacy data are the manufacturer's own studies and an in-vitro synergy figure with SNAP-8; no independent or indexed human trial exists. The course teaches it as 'no independent evidence', not as a mechanism.
claims.reviewNote: was flagged: no primary source; rewritten as an absence-of-evidence statement
claims.gradeDecision: D — rewritten per Omar 2026-09-24 (agreed recommendation)

claims.text: Cosmetic peptides are regulated as cosmetic ingredients, not drugs, and their safety is evaluated by a cosmetics framework rather than a drug-approval pathway.

claims.text: BPC-157 evidence is an extensive rodent literature, largely from one research group, plus uncontrolled human case series. No randomized efficacy trial in people has been published: a 2015 phase 1 safety study and a 2025 single-arm product study posted no results, and the first efficacy RCTs were registered in 2026.
claims.reviewNote: guides rate C (A&RE) — Omar to confirm; two independent 2025–26 reviews now exist
claims.gradeDecision: D — rodent + case series; human RCTs registered 2026, no results

claims.text: TB-500 is the acetylated 17–23 fragment of thymosin β4 (Ac-LKKTETQ), not thymosin β4 itself; the fragment was characterized by analysing the product, and human trial data for the fragment do not exist.

claims.text: SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-1/-3) is the manufacturer's eight-residue extension of the Argireline SNAP-25 mimic. Its efficacy figures come from the manufacturer; the only indexed human studies test it inside multi-ingredient microneedle patches, so no study isolates its effect.

gradingRule: Grade = certainty the source gives for the specific clinical statement the lesson makes, on the guides' A–D scale. A: consistent large RCTs or approval-grade evidence. B: at least one well-designed, adequately powered RCT or an independent, quality-stratified meta-analysis (either direction). C: small or sponsor-funded RCTs without independent replication, or pooled trials dominated by them. D: animal, in-vitro, mechanistic, case series, manufacturer dossiers. 'context' = history, reviews used for framing, trial registrations without results, analytical or regulatory records (regulatory records are primary for status statements, not graded for efficacy). Where the two guides disagree, the lesson states both and the claim takes the grade the primary evidence supports.
authorFindings: A&RE ch.15 ref 4 — 'Sikiric P, et al. Curr Med Chem 2018;25:1972' does not resolve on PubMed; the title matches Curr Pharm Des 2018;24:1990–2001 (PMID 29879879), which the Pocket Guide cites correctly.
PPG-Aug Argireline entry — 'Wang Y et al. [not indexed]': the 2013 Am J Clin Dermatol randomized placebo-controlled trial is indexed (PMID 23417317).
PPG-Aug LL-37 entry — Grönberg et al. is 2014 (printed 2015); Mahlapuu et al. is 2021 (printed 2022).

A&RE ch.15 RUO cautions — the heavy-metal (arsenic, lead) statement has no citation and no primary analytical study of skin-peptide RUO products was found; the course now says 'reported, not documented'. The '30% wrong sequence / 65% endotoxin' figure circulating online traces to no journal.
PPG-Aug KPV entry — the 'small open-label studies for atopic dermatitis' could not be located on PubMed.

GHK-Cu regulatory status — FDA's May 14, 2026 category document records the April 22, 2026 withdrawal, the May 5 partial reinstatement (non-injectable routes) and a PCAC consultation intended before end of February 2027; both guides should date-stamp 'Category 1 (non-injectable)'.

Grade disagreement between the guides — A&RE ch.5 rates Argireline and Matrixyl-type peptides GRADE C; the Pocket Guide rates Argireline, Leuphasyl, Matrixyl 3000 and Palmitoyl Tripeptide-1 GRADE D. The course grades pal-KTTKS and Argireline C (RCTs incl. an independent 2023 trial) and the blends/Leuphasyl D, and names the disagreement.
Oral collagen — Myung & Park 2025 (Am J Med, 23 RCTs) find the benefit only in pharmaceutical-funded and low-quality trials; the author may wish to revisit A&RE's GRADE C.
SNAP-8 is in neither guide; the course adds it from the literature (Errante 2020 review; two combination-product studies).

Not in either guide, worth adding — Miller 2006 (the one indexed RCT of topical GHK-Cu), Aruan 2023 (independent RCT, Argireline vs pal-KTTKS), Esposito 2012 (TB-500 characterized as the Tβ4 17–23 fragment), the two 2026 BPC-157 trial registrations, and the two independent 2025–26 BPC-157 reviews.
